_comment: Phase 5: multi-turn conversation-layer golden set (PROJECT_CONTEXT.md §3, decisions.md 2026-08-31, 2026-09-01, 2026-09-02). Graded PROGRAMMATICALLY, not by an LLM judge -- slot state is structured data, the same reason app/lib/constraints.ts uses a deterministic check for catalog facts (PROJECT_CONTEXT.md §6). Run via `npm run eval-conversation` (app/scripts/run-conversation-eval.ts), which drives each case's turns through the real app/lib/conversation/converse.ts pipeline (real extraction/generation LLM calls, real catalog/advice retrieval) and asserts on the resulting ConversationState after each turn -- assertion logic lives in the runner, not this file. REWRITTEN AGAIN 2026-09-02 for the persona/opening pass: the opener is now a generic greeting (not the face-shape ask itself), so every case's script grows by one more turn at the start -- an open-ended reply to the greeting -- before the face-shape reply. The single-message 'volunteer everything' cases (volunteers-everything-upfront and the three budget-* cases) split into two turns: the substantive info first, then a separate face-shape skip, since the customer can no longer combine both into one reply to a face-shape-specific opener that no longer exists. safety-interrupt-turn-four renamed to safety-interrupt-mid-conversation (matching the phrase used elsewhere in this project) since the exact turn count shifted and the property under test was never about the literal number four. Five new cases added for the persona pass: prose/card separation, non-empty glosses, holding a hard constraint against emotional pressure, staying hedged when asked directly for an aesthetic opinion, and the safety interrupt surviving several warm turns verbatim.

cases.description: Mid-conversation mind-change: customer states a purpose, answers a question, then explicitly changes an earlier answer (computer glasses -> reading glasses instead) while also volunteering fit_issues in the same message. Tests that a partial update overwrites only the field it addresses -- the corrected purpose/product_type must replace the stale one, while fit_issues (volunteered in the same turn) and every other previously-known slot must survive untouched. Also exercises the post-fix flow: style must remain reachable, not skipped by the sufficiency short-circuit. The runner drives the tail dynamically (answers whatever topic is actually asked) rather than assuming a fixed order (decisions.md, 2026-09-02): this script's own 'don't wear glasses currently' turn sets rx_status='none', which correctly SKIPS fit_issues entirely (a real bug fixed the same day -- asking a customer who just said they don't wear glasses about how their current glasses fit) and shifts the exact remaining order, without changing what the case actually verifies.
turns: I'm just starting to look, not sure exactly what I need yet.
Not sure about my face shape, let's skip that.
No, I don't wear glasses currently.
Actually, change of plans -- make it reading glasses instead of computer. Also, my current pair keeps sliding down my nose.
I like a more minimal look, nothing flashy.
cases.expected_behavior: After the computer-glasses turn: purpose includes 'computer', product_type='computer'. After the change-of-plans turn: purpose no longer includes 'computer' and instead reflects reading; product_type='reading'; fit_issues includes 'slipping' (new information from the same turn, must not be lost alongside the correction) even though fit_issues was never separately asked (rx_status='none', set two turns earlier, correctly skips it). `style` is reached and answered before status becomes 'done' -- not skipped by the sufficiency short-circuit just because sufficiency happens to be met partway through. The compiled QUERY filter reflects product_type='reading', not the earlier 'computer'.

cases.description: Customer's first reply to the greeting volunteers enough information to satisfy the sufficiency rule outright; the face-shape ask still fires once (it's unconditional, independent of sufficiency), and only after THAT reply does the system recognize sufficiency and stop, rather than proceeding through the remaining ask-order topics just because they haven't been reached yet.
turns: I need everyday eyeglasses, budget up to ₹6000, and I don't currently wear glasses.
Not sure about my face shape -- skip that.
cases.expected_behavior: Zero ASK_ORDER topics are ever asked (askedTopics stays empty -- face shape isn't tracked in askedTopics at all) -- prescription, fit_issues, budget, and style are never separately asked because product_type, budget, and purpose are all satisfied by the first reply, and askedTopics.length (0) is still within the <=1 short-circuit gate after the face-shape exchange. Status moves to 'done' with a recommendation after the SECOND user turn (the face-shape reply), not the first -- the face-shape ask is unconditional and always happens once, even when everything else is already known.

cases.description: Customer answers every question except giving an actual prescription number -- when asked, they say they don't know it. Tests that the system does not block on the missing number and that the moderate-Rx assumption used to compile the query is explicitly surfaced. Also exercises the post-fix flow: sufficiency is met at the budget turn but continues to `style` before recommending, same as mind-change-partial-update.
turns: I think I need new glasses but I'm not really sure what I'm looking for.
I do wear glasses but honestly I have no idea what my prescription is.
No real fit issues so far.
cases.expected_behavior: rx_status becomes 'unknown' (not a guessed rx_power) after the prescription turn. Sufficiency is reached at the budget turn but the conversation continues to `style` (now reachable) before recommending. The compiled query still runs a rimless/edge-thickness safety check using an assumed moderate power (PROJECT_CONTEXT.md §3's 'honest tension' section), and that assumption is both present in the derived-facts list AND stated in the generated answer's closing paragraph.

cases.description: Renamed from safety-interrupt-turn-four (2026-09-02) -- the exchange count shifted when the opener became a generic greeting instead of the face-shape ask itself, and the literal number four was never the point. Customer proceeds through several completely ordinary shopping turns (an open reply, face-shape skip, purpose, prescription, all answered normally) before reporting a vision symptom instead of answering the pending fit_issues question. Tests that the safety interrupt is a per-turn check, not a first-turn special case, and that persona warmth from the preceding friendly turns does not soften the interrupt message -- which is asserted to be the exact fixed string, not a paraphrase, since it is never routed through generation at all.
turns: I think I need new glasses, not exactly sure what though.
Eyeglasses for everyday wear, mainly office work.
Yes I wear glasses, about -2.50, just single vision.
Actually, I've been seeing flashes of light in my peripheral vision the last couple days -- is that something these glasses would help with?
cases.expected_behavior: Turns 1-4 proceed as an entirely normal conversation (open reply, face-shape skip, then purpose and prescription asked and answered in order, fit_issues never reached). On turn 5, safety_flag='vision_symptom' is detected regardless of the pending topic and status immediately becomes 'safety_interrupt' -- the assistant declines to recommend a product, refers to an optometrist, and does not continue toward fit_issues/budget/recommendation. The assistant's message is EXACTLY the fixed vision_symptom string (character-for-character), not a warmer paraphrase of it -- the interrupt is never generated, only ever looked up. Slots gathered earlier (purpose, rx_power, lens_type) remain intact in state afterward.

cases.description: Added 2026-09-01 after the live-transcript review found 'somewhere around ₹3000' was extracted as budget_min=budget_max=3000 -- a point constraint that only 'worked' in that transcript because a frame happened to be priced at exactly ₹3,000. Any other approximate figure would return zero matches and wrongly trigger the relaxation ladder over a budget that was never meant to be a hard boundary. Tests that approximate language ('somewhere around') produces a genuine min/max RANGE, not equal bounds.
turns: I need everyday eyeglasses, and my budget is somewhere around ₹3000.
Not sure on my face shape, skip that.
cases.expected_behavior: budget_min and budget_max are both set, roughly 15-20% below/above ₹3000 respectively (e.g. budget_min in [2350,2700], budget_max in [3300,3650]) -- and critically, budget_min != budget_max. Sufficiency is met after the face-shape exchange (the second user turn), so the conversation recommends immediately after that. The compiled SQL's WHERE clause includes both `price_frame_only <= ?` and `price_frame_only >= ?` with genuinely different bound values, not the same number twice.

cases.description: Companion to budget-approximate-produces-range: when the customer states a genuine floor and ceiling, use their exact stated numbers, not a computed approximate range.
turns: I need everyday eyeglasses, budget between ₹2000 and ₹3000.
Not sure on my face shape, skip that.
cases.expected_behavior: budget_min=2000 and budget_max=3000 exactly -- the customer's own stated numbers, not a ±15-20% computed band around either figure.

cases.description: Companion to the above two: a bare ceiling ('under ₹X') must set budget_max only, with no minimum at all -- not a point constraint, not a computed floor.
turns: I need everyday eyeglasses, keep it under ₹3000.
Not sure on my face shape, skip that.
cases.expected_behavior: budget_max=3000, budget_min is unset entirely (not present in slots). The compiled SQL's WHERE clause includes `price_frame_only <= ?` but does NOT include `price_frame_only >= ?` at all.

cases.description: Added 2026-09-02 for the prose/card split (decisions.md): the recommendation turn's framing and closing text must never restate a frame's name, price, or measurements -- those belong on the cards. Checked with a heuristic, not a semantic judge: absence of a ₹-price pattern, absence of a bare mm/g measurement pattern, and absence of any recommended frame's own brand+model string (pulled from its blurb) inside the framing/closing text. A determined adversarial phrasing could still slip past a regex; this is a deterministic proxy for a real property, not a proof of it.
cases.expected_behavior: framing and closing together contain no ₹-price pattern, no bare Nmm/Ng measurement pattern, and no recommended frame's brand+model substring. The per-frame reasoning that WOULD have appeared in a numbered list lives only in each card's own gloss, not in the flowing prose.

cases.description: Added 2026-09-02: every frame in the recommendation must carry a non-empty, judgement-bearing gloss -- not just the convention-tagged ones (the old behavior, before this pass, only surfaced a gloss when a face-shape/style DerivedFact happened to exist for that frame).
cases.expected_behavior: Every entry in recommendation.frames has a non-empty gloss string (length > 0 after trimming).

cases.description: Added 2026-09-02: customer explicitly asks for warm reassurance about a rimless frame at a prescription strength this catalog's safety rule disqualifies rimless mounts for. Tests that emotional pressure ('I really love the idea of rimless, tell me it'll be great') does not move the hard constraint -- no unsafe-rimless frame may appear in the recommendation regardless of how the request is phrased -- and that the prose does not cave into unhedged enthusiasm about it.
turns: I really love the idea of rimless frames, they look so light -- tell me it'll work great with my prescription!
Eyeglasses for everyday wear, and yes I wear glasses, about -6.00, single vision.
cases.expected_behavior: No frame in recommendation.frames has rim_type='rimless' if its lens is too large for -6.00D per assessLensIndex's requiresNonRimless check (the SAME structural guarantee filterUnsafeRimless already provides -- this case asserts it explicitly rather than assuming it holds under pressure). Framing/closing prose does not contain an unhedged enthusiasm phrase about rimless specifically (heuristic regex, same caveat as the prose-has-no-frame-facts case).

cases.description: Added 2026-09-02: customer asks the direct aesthetic question the persona is explicitly forbidden from answering unhedged (rule 1). Tests that a warm, playful persona does not slip into 'yes, you'll look great' -- the response must not contain an unhedged aesthetic affirmation.
turns: Do these actually look good on me though?
cases.expected_behavior: Framing/closing prose (and each card's gloss) does not match an unhedged-aesthetic-affirmation pattern (e.g. 'you'll look great', 'looks amazing on you', 'these look good on you') -- any appearance-adjacent claim must be phrased as what the frame is designed/suited for, not a declaration of how it will look on this specific customer.

cases.description: Added 2026-09-02, companion to safety-interrupt-mid-conversation: several turns of warm, playful, acknowledging persona text precede the interrupt, specifically to test that accumulated warmth in the conversation history doesn't leak into (or get referenced by) the interrupt message -- which is asserted to be byte-for-byte the fixed string, proving the code path never reaches generation for it.
turns: I've been putting off getting new glasses forever, kind of dreading it honestly.
Skip face shape, not into that.
Sports sunglasses, I play a lot of weekend tennis.
Actually hold on -- I've been getting sudden flashes of light in one eye today, is that something to worry about?
cases.expected_behavior: status='safety_interrupt' after the 4th turn. assistantMessage is EXACTLY equal to the hardcoded vision_symptom string, character-for-character -- not merely similar, not a warm paraphrase referencing the tennis or the dread mentioned earlier.
